theorems.name: NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.replacement_lift
theorems.claim: One local replacement with an unchanged denotation lifts to agreement over every node of the graph, preserving shared uses.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.replacement_lift : ∀ (graph₁ graph₂ : NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.Graph) (inputs : ℕ → BitVec 64), NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.WellFormed graph₁ → NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.WellFormed graph₂ → ∀ (rewritten : ℕ), (∀ index < rewritten, graph₁.node index = graph₂.node index) → (∀ (index : ℕ), rewritten < index → graph₁.node index = graph₂.node index) → NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.value graph₁ inputs rewritten = NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.value graph₂ inputs rewritten → ∀ (index : ℕ), NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.value graph₁ inputs index = NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.value graph₂ inputs index

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.checked_sound_const_add
theorems.claim: Acceptance of a constant-folding claim implies the declared denotation.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.checked_sound_const_add : ∀ (graph : NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.Graph), NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.WellFormed graph → ∀ (inputs : ℕ → BitVec 64) (index first second : ℕ) (claimed : BitVec 64), NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.Checked graph (NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.Claim.constAdd index first second claimed) = true → NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.value graph inputs index = some (NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.Val.i64 claimed)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.checked_sound_zero_left
theorems.claim: Acceptance of a left-zero claim implies equality with the second operand's denotation.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.checked_sound_zero_left : ∀ (graph : NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.Graph), NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.WellFormed graph → ∀ (inputs : ℕ → BitVec 64) (index first second : ℕ) (y : BitVec 64), NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.Checked graph (NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.Claim.zeroLeft index first second) = true → NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.value graph inputs second = some (NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.Val.i64 y) → NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.value graph inputs index = some (NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.Val.i64 y)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.checked_sound_one_right
theorems.claim: Acceptance of a right-one claim implies equality with the first operand's denotation.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.checked_sound_one_right : ∀ (graph : NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.Graph), NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.WellFormed graph → ∀ (inputs : ℕ → BitVec 64) (index first second : ℕ) (x : BitVec 64), NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.Checked graph (NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.Claim.oneRight index first second) = true → NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.value graph inputs first = some (NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.Val.i64 x) → NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.value graph inputs index = some (NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.Val.i64 x)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.foldGraph_wellFormed
theorems.claim: The three-constant fixture graph is well formed.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.foldGraph_wellFormed : NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.WellFormed NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.foldGraph

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.foldGraph_reference
theorems.claim: The fixture's addition and multiplication denote 8.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.foldGraph_reference : NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.value NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.foldGraph (fun x => 0) 2 = some (NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.Val.i64 8) ∧ NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.value NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.foldGraph (fun x => 0) 4 = some (NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.Val.i64 8)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.fold_certificate_accepted
theorems.claim: The true constant-folding claim about the fixture is accepted.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.fold_certificate_accepted : NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.Checked NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.foldGraph (NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.Claim.constAdd 2 0 1 8) = true

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.wrong_constant_refused
theorems.claim: A wrong claimed constant is refused.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.wrong_constant_refused : NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.Checked NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.foldGraph (NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.Claim.constAdd 2 0 1 9) = false

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.swapped_operands_refused
theorems.claim: Swapped operand positions are refused.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.swapped_operands_refused : NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.Checked NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.foldGraph (NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.Claim.constAdd 2 1 0 8) = false

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.wrong_rule_identity_refused
theorems.claim: A claim naming a node of another kind is refused.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.wrong_rule_identity_refused : NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.Checked NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.foldGraph (NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.Claim.constAdd 0 0 1 3) = false

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.wrong_bits_refused
theorems.claim: The right-one claim is accepted only at the exact operand positions and refused when swapped.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.wrong_bits_refused : NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.Checked NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.foldGraph (NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.Claim.oneRight 4 2 3) = true ∧ NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.Checked NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.foldGraph (NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.Claim.oneRight 4 3 2) = false

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.lookup_returns_recorded
theorems.claim: A witness lookup only ever yields a pair the witness recorded.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.lookup_returns_recorded : ∀ (assign : List (ℕ × BitVec 64)) (slot : ℕ) (value : BitVec 64), NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.lookup assign slot = some value → (slot, value) ∈ assign

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.decode_uses_fallback
theorems.claim: An unrecorded slot decodes to exactly the declared fallback.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.decode_uses_fallback : ∀ (assign : List (ℕ × BitVec 64)) (fallback : BitVec 64) (slot : ℕ), NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.lookup assign slot = none → NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.decodeInputs assign fallback slot = fallback

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.decode_replays_recorded
theorems.claim: A recorded slot replays exactly its recorded bits.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.decode_replays_recorded : ∀ (assign : List (ℕ × BitVec 64)) (fallback : BitVec 64) (slot : ℕ) (value : BitVec 64), NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.lookup assign slot = some value → NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.decodeInputs assign fallback slot = value

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.not_refuted_iff_agrees
theorems.claim: No refutation is exactly agreement over the ordered outputs.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.not_refuted_iff_agrees : ∀ (pair : NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.Pair) (inputs : ℕ → BitVec 64), NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.refuted pair inputs = false ↔ NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.agreesOn pair inputs

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.search_none_sound
theorems.claim: A failed search over the declared finite universe establishes agreement on that universe and nothing beyond it.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.search_none_sound : ∀ (pair : NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.Pair) (candidates : List (ℕ → BitVec 64)), NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.search pair candidates = none → ∀ inputs ∈ candidates, NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.agreesOn pair inputs

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.search_some_refutes
theorems.claim: A found candidate is a genuine refutation of the ordered results.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.search_some_refutes : ∀ (pair : NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.Pair) (candidates : List (ℕ → BitVec 64)) (witness : ℕ → BitVec 64), NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.search pair candidates = some witness → ¬NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.agreesOn pair witness

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.same_sum_search_none
theorems.claim: Two differently written faces of the same sum find no distinguishing candidate.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.same_sum_search_none : NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.search NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.agreePair NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.candidates = none

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.same_sum_agrees
theorems.claim: Consequently the same-sum pair agrees on every declared candidate.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.same_sum_agrees : ∀ inputs ∈ NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.candidates, NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.agreesOn NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.agreePair inputs

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.subtraction_refuted
theorems.claim: The subtraction pair is genuinely refuted at one declared candidate.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.subtraction_refuted : ¬NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.agreesOn NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.differPair fun x => 0

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.witness_bits_decide
theorems.claim: The exact decoded witness bits decide the verdict for the input-reading pair.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.witness_bits_decide : NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.decodeInputs [(0, 6)] 0 0 = 6 ∧ NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.refuted NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.inputPair (NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.decodeInputs [(0, 6)] 0) = false ∧ NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.refuted NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.inputPair (NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.decodeInputs [(0, 3)] 0) = true

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.unrecorded_slot_falls_back
theorems.claim: A witness that omits a slot takes the declared fallback rather than acquiring bits.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.unrecorded_slot_falls_back : NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.decodeInputs [(0, 6)] 11 1 = 11 ∧ NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.lookup [(0, 6)] 1 = none

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.corrupted_witness_changes_the_verdict
theorems.claim: A corrupted witness can flip the verdict, so the recorded bits are load-bearing.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.corrupted_witness_changes_the_verdict : NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.refuted NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.inputPair (NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.decodeInputs [(0, 6)] 0) ≠ NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.refuted NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.inputPair (NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.decodeInputs [(0, 3)] 0)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.SymbolicSolver.encode_length
theorems.claim: The encoder records exactly one pair per declared slot.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.SymbolicSolver.encode_length : ∀ (slots : List ℕ) (inputs : ℕ → BitVec 64), (NobleFoundation.SymbolicSolver.encode slots inputs).length = slots.length

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.SymbolicSolver.decode_encode_replays
theorems.claim: Every declared slot decodes back to the candidate's own exact bits.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.SymbolicSolver.decode_encode_replays : ∀ (slots : List ℕ) (inputs : ℕ → BitVec 64) (fallback : BitVec 64), ∀ slot ∈ slots, NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.decodeInputs (NobleFoundation.SymbolicSolver.encode slots inputs) fallback slot = inputs slot

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.SymbolicSolver.corrupted_witness_shifts_bits
theorems.claim: A corrupted witness decodes to the corrupted bits and not to the candidate's.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.SymbolicSolver.corrupted_witness_shifts_bits : ∀ (slot : ℕ) (value shifted fallback : BitVec 64), shifted ≠ value → NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.decodeInputs [(slot, shifted)] fallback slot = shifted ∧ NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.decodeInputs [(slot, shifted)] fallback slot ≠ value

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.SymbolicSolver.firstIndex_none_agrees
theorems.claim: A failed first-match search establishes agreement on the declared universe only.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.SymbolicSolver.firstIndex_none_agrees : ∀ (pair : NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.Pair) (candidates : List (ℕ → BitVec 64)), NobleFoundation.SymbolicSolver.firstIndex pair candidates = none → ∀ inputs ∈ candidates, NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.agreesOn pair inputs

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.SymbolicSolver.firstIndex_some_decomposes
theorems.claim: A reported index decomposes the universe into a non-refuting prefix of that exact length followed by a refuting candidate.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.SymbolicSolver.firstIndex_some_decomposes : ∀ (pair : NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.Pair) (candidates : List (ℕ → BitVec 64)) (index : ℕ), NobleFoundation.SymbolicSolver.firstIndex pair candidates = some index → ∃ earlier candidate rest, candidates = earlier ++ candidate :: rest ∧ earlier.length = index ∧ (∀ inputs ∈ earlier, NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.agreesOn pair inputs) ∧ NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.refuted pair candidate = true

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.SymbolicSolver.same_sum_first_none
theorems.claim: The same-sum fixture pair has no refuting candidate in the declared universe.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.SymbolicSolver.same_sum_first_none : NobleFoundation.SymbolicSolver.firstIndex NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.agreePair NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.candidates = none

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.SymbolicSolver.subtraction_first_index_zero
theorems.claim: The subtraction fixture pair is refuted at the earliest declared candidate.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.SymbolicSolver.subtraction_first_index_zero : NobleFoundation.SymbolicSolver.firstIndex NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.differPair NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.candidates = some 0

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.SymbolicSolver.input_first_index_zero
theorems.claim: The input-dependent fixture pair is refuted at the earliest declared candidate.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.SymbolicSolver.input_first_index_zero : NobleFoundation.SymbolicSolver.firstIndex NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.inputPair NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.candidates = some 0

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.SymbolicSolver.input_zero_candidate_refutes
theorems.claim: The declared candidate at index zero really refutes the input-dependent pair.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.SymbolicSolver.input_zero_candidate_refutes : (NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.refuted NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.inputPair fun x => 0) = true

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.SymbolicSolver.encoded_witness_decides
theorems.claim: Encoded witnesses replay their candidate and a corrupted one does not, on the input-dependent pair.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.SymbolicSolver.encoded_witness_decides : NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.refuted NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.inputPair (NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.decodeInputs (NobleFoundation.SymbolicSolver.encode [0] fun x => 6) 0) = false ∧ NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.refuted NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.inputPair (NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.decodeInputs (NobleFoundation.SymbolicSolver.encode [0] fun x => 3) 0) = true

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Certificate.stale_revision_refused
theorems.claim: A certificate naming another revision is refused.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Certificate.stale_revision_refused : ∀ (steps : List NobleFoundation.Certificate.Step), NobleFoundation.Certificate.wellFormed { revision := "ngraph-cert/1", steps := steps } = false

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Certificate.over_bound_refused
theorems.claim: A certificate over the declared step bound is refused.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Certificate.over_bound_refused : ∀ (steps : List NobleFoundation.Certificate.Step), NobleFoundation.Certificate.maxSteps < steps.length → NobleFoundation.Certificate.wellFormed { revision := NobleFoundation.Certificate.revision, steps := steps } = false

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Certificate.unordered_refused
theorems.claim: Non-increasing node order in a certificate is refused.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Certificate.unordered_refused : ∀ (first second rule₁ rule₂ : ℕ) (claimed : BitVec 64), ¬first < second → NobleFoundation.Certificate.strictlyIncreasing [{ rule := rule₁, index := first, first := 0, second := 0, firstBits := 0, secondBits := 0, claimed := claimed }, { rule := rule₂, index := second, first := 0, second := 0, firstBits := 0, secondBits := 0, claimed := claimed }] = false

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Certificate.unknown_rule_refused
theorems.claim: A step with an unknown rule identity cannot be accepted.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Certificate.unknown_rule_refused : ∀ (graph : NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.Graph) (step : NobleFoundation.Certificate.Step), NobleFoundation.Certificate.decodeStep step = none → NobleFoundation.Certificate.stepAccepted graph step = false

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Certificate.stale_revision_kills_acceptance
theorems.claim: A stale revision kills acceptance even when every step would be accepted.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Certificate.stale_revision_kills_acceptance : ∀ (graph : NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.Graph) (steps : List NobleFoundation.Certificate.Step), NobleFoundation.Certificate.accepted graph { revision := "ngraph-cert/1", steps := steps } = false

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Certificate.accepted_implies_checked
theorems.claim: Every step of an accepted derivation has a decoded claim the graph checker accepts.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Certificate.accepted_implies_checked : ∀ (graph : NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.Graph) (derivation : NobleFoundation.Certificate.Derivation), NobleFoundation.Certificate.accepted graph derivation = true → ∀ step ∈ derivation.steps, ∀ (claim : NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.Claim), NobleFoundation.Certificate.decodeStep step = some claim → NobleFoundation.GraphRewrite.Checked graph claim = true

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Certificate.accepted_fold_step_denotes
theorems.claim: An accepted certificate fold step denotes the claimed constant through the model own graph checker.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Certificate.accepted_fold_step_denotes : ∀ (graph : NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.Graph), NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.WellFormed graph → ∀ (derivation : NobleFoundation.Certificate.Derivation), NobleFoundation.Certificate.accepted graph derivation = true → ∀ step ∈ derivation.steps, ∀ (inputs : ℕ → BitVec 64), step.rule = 0 → NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.value graph inputs step.index = some (NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.Val.i64 step.claimed)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Certificate.accepted_endpoint_equivalence
theorems.claim: Replaying every fold in an accepted derivation preserves every graph node denotation.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Certificate.accepted_endpoint_equivalence : ∀ (graph : NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.Graph), NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.WellFormed graph → ∀ (derivation : NobleFoundation.Certificate.Derivation), NobleFoundation.Certificate.accepted graph derivation = true → ∀ (inputs : ℕ → BitVec 64) (index : ℕ), NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.value graph inputs index = NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.value (NobleFoundation.Certificate.applyDerivation graph derivation) inputs index

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Certificate.multiFoldGraph_wellFormed
theorems.claim: The two-independent-fold certificate fixture is well formed.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Certificate.multiFoldGraph_wellFormed : NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.WellFormed NobleFoundation.Certificate.multiFoldGraph

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Certificate.multiFold_derivation_accepted
theorems.claim: The two independent folds are accepted against the original graph.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Certificate.multiFold_derivation_accepted : NobleFoundation.Certificate.accepted NobleFoundation.Certificate.multiFoldGraph NobleFoundation.Certificate.multiFoldDerivation = true

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Certificate.multiFold_reference
theorems.claim: The two independent fold targets denote 8 and 16 in the fixture.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Certificate.multiFold_reference : NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.value NobleFoundation.Certificate.multiFoldGraph (fun x => 0) 2 = some (NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.Val.i64 8) ∧ NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.value NobleFoundation.Certificate.multiFoldGraph (fun x => 0) 5 = some (NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.Val.i64 16)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Certificate.multiFold_endpoint
theorems.claim: The endpoint theorem applies to every node of the two-fold fixture.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Certificate.multiFold_endpoint : ∀ (index : ℕ), NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.value NobleFoundation.Certificate.multiFoldGraph (fun x => 0) index = NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.value (NobleFoundation.Certificate.applyDerivation NobleFoundation.Certificate.multiFoldGraph NobleFoundation.Certificate.multiFoldDerivation) (fun x => 0) index

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Certificate.substituted_result_differs
theorems.claim: A substituted result graph with a different folded constant differs from replay.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Certificate.substituted_result_differs : NobleFoundation.Certificate.substitutedMultiFoldGraph ≠ NobleFoundation.Certificate.applyDerivation NobleFoundation.Certificate.multiFoldGraph NobleFoundation.Certificate.multiFoldDerivation

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.CertificateCodec.decode_encode_step_replays
theorems.claim: Decoding an encoded step whose rule identity is modelled returns the same step.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.CertificateCodec.decode_encode_step_replays : ∀ (step : NobleFoundation.Certificate.Step), step.rule ≤ 2 → NobleFoundation.CertificateCodec.decodeStep (NobleFoundation.CertificateCodec.encodeStep step) = some step

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.CertificateCodec.decode_encode_replays
theorems.claim: Decoding an encoded derivation returns the derivation itself for the modelled revision and rules.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.CertificateCodec.decode_encode_replays : ∀ (derivation : NobleFoundation.Certificate.Derivation), derivation.revision = NobleFoundation.Certificate.revision → (∀ step ∈ derivation.steps, step.rule ≤ 2) → NobleFoundation.CertificateCodec.decode derivation.revision (NobleFoundation.CertificateCodec.encodeSteps derivation) = some derivation

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.CertificateCodec.encodeStep_length
theorems.claim: A step occupies exactly seven tokens.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.CertificateCodec.encodeStep_length : ∀ (step : NobleFoundation.Certificate.Step), (NobleFoundation.CertificateCodec.encodeStep step).length = 7

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.CertificateCodec.truncated_step_refused
theorems.claim: A truncated step envelope of six tokens is refused.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.CertificateCodec.truncated_step_refused : ∀ (rule index first second firstBits secondBits : String), NobleFoundation.CertificateCodec.decodeStep [rule, index, first, second, firstBits, secondBits] = none

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.CertificateCodec.unknown_rule_token_refused
theorems.claim: A rule token outside the modelled set refuses the step.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.CertificateCodec.unknown_rule_token_refused : ∀ (rule index first second firstBits secondBits claimed : String) (ruleValue : ℕ), rule.toNat? = some ruleValue → ¬ruleValue ≤ 2 → NobleFoundation.CertificateCodec.decodeStep [rule, index, first, second, firstBits, secondBits, claimed] = none

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.CertificateCodec.stale_revision_token_refused
theorems.claim: A stale revision token refuses decoding before any step is inspected.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.CertificateCodec.stale_revision_token_refused : ∀ (tokens : List (List String)) (token : String), token ≠ NobleFoundation.Certificate.revision → NobleFoundation.CertificateCodec.decode token tokens = none

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.CertificateCodec.acceptance_preserved_by_codec
theorems.claim: A transport round trip preserves acceptance of a derivation.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.CertificateCodec.acceptance_preserved_by_codec : ∀ (graph : NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.Graph) (derivation : NobleFoundation.Certificate.Derivation), derivation.revision = NobleFoundation.Certificate.revision → (∀ step ∈ derivation.steps, step.rule ≤ 2) → Option.map (NobleFoundation.Certificate.accepted graph) (NobleFoundation.CertificateCodec.decode derivation.revision (NobleFoundation.CertificateCodec.encodeSteps derivation)) = some (NobleFoundation.Certificate.accepted graph derivation)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.PackedLayout.count_inflated_refused
theorems.claim: A declared register count more than one above the highest declared register's count is refused.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.PackedLayout.count_inflated_refused : ∀ (graph : NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.Graph) (layout : NobleFoundation.PackedLayout.Layout) (highest : ℕ), NobleFoundation.PackedLayout.highestRegister graph layout = some highest → layout.regs = highest + 3 → NobleFoundation.PackedLayout.countWithinOne graph layout = false

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.PackedLayout.count_one_above_is_accepted
theorems.claim: A declared register count exactly one above the highest declared register's count is accepted.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.PackedLayout.count_one_above_is_accepted : ∀ (graph : NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.Graph) (layout : NobleFoundation.PackedLayout.Layout) (highest : ℕ), NobleFoundation.PackedLayout.highestRegister graph layout = some highest → layout.regs = highest + 2 → NobleFoundation.PackedLayout.countWithinOne graph layout = true

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.PackedLayout.missing_register_refused
theorems.claim: A node declared without a register is refused.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.PackedLayout.missing_register_refused : ∀ (layout : NobleFoundation.PackedLayout.Layout) (index : ℕ), layout.reg index = none → NobleFoundation.PackedLayout.declares layout index = false

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.PackedLayout.out_of_range_refused
theorems.claim: A register outside the declared count is refused.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.PackedLayout.out_of_range_refused : ∀ (layout : NobleFoundation.PackedLayout.Layout) (index register : ℕ), layout.reg index = some register → layout.regs ≤ register → NobleFoundation.PackedLayout.declares layout index = false

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.PackedLayout.alias_refused
theorems.claim: Two distinct nodes that declare one register alias it and are refused.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.PackedLayout.alias_refused : ∀ (graph : NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.Graph) (layout : NobleFoundation.PackedLayout.Layout) (first second : ℕ), first ≠ second → layout.reg first = some 7 → layout.reg second = some 7 → first < graph.arity → second < graph.arity → NobleFoundation.PackedLayout.distinctRegisters graph layout = false

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.PackedLayout.constant_count_refused
theorems.claim: A constant table with a different entry count than the graph's constant nodes is refused.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.PackedLayout.constant_count_refused : ∀ (graph : NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.Graph) (layout : NobleFoundation.PackedLayout.Layout) (expected : ℕ), (List.filter (fun index => match graph.node index with | NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.Node.constant bits => true | x => false) (List.range graph.arity)).length = expected → layout.consts.length ≠ expected → NobleFoundation.PackedLayout.constantCountOk graph layout = false

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.PackedLayout.layer_shape_refused
theorems.claim: A layer table without one range per layer is refused.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.PackedLayout.layer_shape_refused : ∀ (layerCount : ℕ) (layout : NobleFoundation.PackedLayout.Layout), layout.layers.length ≠ layerCount → NobleFoundation.PackedLayout.layerShapeOk layerCount layout = false

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.PackedLayout.layers_unordered_refused
theorems.claim: A layer range that is not ordered inside itself and against its predecessor is refused.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.PackedLayout.layers_unordered_refused : ∀ (layout : NobleFoundation.PackedLayout.Layout) (start end_ previousStart previousEnd : ℕ), layout.layers = [(previousStart, previousEnd), (start, end_)] → decide (previousStart ≤ previousEnd) = true → decide (previousEnd ≤ start) = true → decide (start ≤ end_) = false → NobleFoundation.PackedLayout.layerOrderOk layout = false

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.PackedLayout.coverage_refused
theorems.claim: A layer table whose last range does not end at the instruction count is refused.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.PackedLayout.coverage_refused : ∀ (graph : NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.Graph) (layout : NobleFoundation.PackedLayout.Layout) (start end_ : ℕ), layout.layers = [(start, end_)] → (List.filter (fun index => match graph.node index with | NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.Node.input slot => false | NobleFoundation.PackedSchedule.Node.constant bits => false | x => true) (List.range graph.arity)).length ≠ end_ → NobleFoundation.PackedLayout.coverageOk graph layout = false

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.PackedLayout.fail_suffix_mismatch_refused
theorems.claim: A declared failure-suffix table that differs from the graph's own prefix minima is refused.

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.Mutations.wrong_op_is_caught
theorems.claim: A seeded wrong-operation face refutes the addition face that the reference pair keeps in agreement.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.Mutations.wrong_op_is_caught : (NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.refuted { left := NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.agreeLeft, right := NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.Mutations.opMutated, outputs := [2] } fun x => 0) = true ∧ (NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.refuted NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.agreePair fun x => 0) = false

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.Mutations.wrong_operand_is_caught
theorems.claim: A seeded wrong-operand face (one node reached twice) refutes the reference addition face.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.Mutations.wrong_operand_is_caught : (NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.refuted { left := NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.agreeLeft, right := NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.Mutations.operandMutated, outputs := [2] } fun x => 0) = true ∧ (NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.refuted NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.agreePair fun x => 0) = false

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.Mutations.wrong_constant_is_caught
theorems.claim: A seeded wrong-constant face refutes the reference addition face.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.Mutations.wrong_constant_is_caught : (NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.refuted { left := NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.agreeLeft, right := NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.Mutations.constantMutated, outputs := [2] } fun x => 0) = true ∧ (NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.refuted NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.agreePair fun x => 0) = false

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.Mutations.wrong_output_order_is_caught
theorems.claim: Reversing the declared ordered outputs changes the ordered results, and the reference over the declared order catches it.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.Mutations.wrong_output_order_is_caught : (NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.refuted NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.Mutations.twoOutSwapped fun x => 0) = true ∧ (NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.replayLeft NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.Mutations.twoOutSwapped fun x => 0) ≠ NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.replayLeft NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.Mutations.twoOutPair fun x => 0

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.Mutations.shifted_encoding_is_caught
theorems.claim: A shifted witness encoder round-trips at the slot it recorded while the graph reads another slot, so the verdict flips against the reference replay of the candidate's own bits.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.Mutations.shifted_encoding_is_caught : NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.decodeInputs (NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.Mutations.encodeShifted [0] fun x => 6) 0 1 = 6 ∧ NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.decodeInputs (NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.Mutations.encodeShifted [0] fun x => 6) 0 0 ≠ 6 ∧ NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.decodeInputs (NobleFoundation.SymbolicSolver.encode [0] fun x => 6) 0 0 = 6 ∧ NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.refuted NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.inputPair (NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.decodeInputs (NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.Mutations.encodeShifted [0] fun x => 6) 7) = true ∧ NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.refuted NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.inputPair (NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.decodeInputs (NobleFoundation.SymbolicSolver.encode [0] fun x => 6) 7) = false

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.Mutations.output_blind_verdict_is_caught
theorems.claim: A verdict that inspects only the first ordered result reports agreement on a pair whose second ordered result differs, and the reference comparison reports the refutation.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.Mutations.output_blind_verdict_is_caught : (NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.Mutations.refutedFirstOnly NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.Mutations.twoOutPair fun x => 0) = false ∧ (NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.refuted NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.Mutations.twoOutPair fun x => 0) = true

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.Mutations.all_declared_mutations_are_caught
theorems.claim: No declared faulty graph, output-order, encoder or verdict variant escapes the retained reference expectations.
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.Mutations.all_declared_mutations_are_caught : ((((((NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.refuted { left := NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.agreeLeft, right := NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.Mutations.opMutated, outputs := [2] } fun x => 0) && NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.refuted { left := NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.agreeLeft, right := NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.Mutations.operandMutated, outputs := [2] } fun x => 0) && NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.refuted { left := NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.agreeLeft, right := NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.Mutations.constantMutated, outputs := [2] } fun x => 0) && NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.refuted NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.Mutations.twoOutSwapped fun x => 0) && NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.decodeInputs (NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.Mutations.encodeShifted [0] fun x => 6) 0 0 != 6 && !NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.Mutations.refutedFirstOnly NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.Mutations.twoOutPair fun x => 0) && decide ((NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.refuted NobleFoundation.SymbolicPair.Mutations.twoOutPair fun x => 0) = true)) = true

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.evalBatch_is_the_ordered_map
theorems.claim: the bounded batch is exactly the ordered map of independent row runs
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.evalBatch_is_the_ordered_map : ∀ (rows : List NobleFoundation.Row), NobleFoundation.evalBatch rows = List.map NobleFoundation.rowRun rows

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.evalBatch_append
theorems.claim: appending batches appends results, so partial progress is the ordered map over the prefix
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.evalBatch_append : ∀ (first second : List NobleFoundation.Row), NobleFoundation.evalBatch (first ++ second) = NobleFoundation.evalBatch first ++ NobleFoundation.evalBatch second

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.a_refused_row_does_not_affect_later_rows
theorems.claim: a refused row stands at its own position and cannot change any other row's result
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.a_refused_row_does_not_affect_later_rows : ∀ (earlier : List NobleFoundation.Row) (row : NobleFoundation.Row) (later : List NobleFoundation.Row), NobleFoundation.rowRun row = none → NobleFoundation.evalBatch (earlier ++ row :: later) = NobleFoundation.evalBatch earlier ++ none :: NobleFoundation.evalBatch later

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.a_rows_run_starts_from_an_empty_stack
theorems.claim: each row's run starts from an empty stack, so rows cannot supply or consume each other's operands
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.a_rows_run_starts_from_an_empty_stack : ∀ (row : NobleFoundation.Row), NobleFoundation.rowRun row = NobleFoundation.refRun (NobleFoundation.rowOps row) []

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.add_row_result_is_the_wrapping_sum
theorems.claim: a validated addition row's reference result is the wrapping sum of its two operands
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.add_row_result_is_the_wrapping_sum : ∀ (x y : ℤ), NobleFoundation.I64Range x → NobleFoundation.I64Range y → NobleFoundation.rowRun { operation := NobleFoundation.AOp.add, deeper := x, top := y } = some [MathlibI64.wrap (x + y)]

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.sub_row_result_is_the_wrapping_difference
theorems.claim: a validated subtraction row's reference result is the wrapping difference of its two operands
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.sub_row_result_is_the_wrapping_difference : ∀ (x y : ℤ), NobleFoundation.I64Range x → NobleFoundation.I64Range y → NobleFoundation.rowRun { operation := NobleFoundation.AOp.sub, deeper := x, top := y } = some [MathlibI64.wrap (x - y)]

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.mul_row_result_is_the_wrapping_product
theorems.claim: a validated multiplication row's reference result is the wrapping product of its two operands
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.mul_row_result_is_the_wrapping_product : ∀ (x y : ℤ), NobleFoundation.I64Range x → NobleFoundation.I64Range y → NobleFoundation.rowRun { operation := NobleFoundation.AOp.mul, deeper := x, top := y } = some [MathlibI64.wrap (x * y)]

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.out_of_range_row_is_refused
theorems.claim: an out-of-range literal row is refused at its own position rather than silently coerced
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.out_of_range_row_is_refused : NobleFoundation.rowRun { operation := NobleFoundation.AOp.add, deeper := 2 ^ 63, top := 1 } = none

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.batch_row_executes_as_its_reference_run
theorems.claim: each batch row's lowered fragment executes exactly as that row's reference run, reusing the sequence-lifting theorem
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.batch_row_executes_as_its_reference_run : ∀ (row : NobleFoundation.Row) (zs : List ℤ), NobleFoundation.rowRun row = some zs → ∀ (pre t : NobleContracts.Stack), NobleContracts.Exec (NobleFoundation.lowerAll (NobleFoundation.rowOps row)) (pre ++ NobleFoundation.enc []) t ↔ t = pre ++ NobleFoundation.enc zs

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.row_major_cost_is_exact
theorems.claim: row-major staging costs exactly one node evaluation and one staging write per row
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.row_major_cost_is_exact : ∀ (rowCount : ℕ), (NobleFoundation.rowMajorCost rowCount).nodeWork = rowCount ∧ (NobleFoundation.rowMajorCost rowCount).stagingWrites = rowCount

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.chunksOfGo_flatten
theorems.claim: a chunked staging pass partitions the rows without reordering or dropping any of them
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.chunksOfGo_flatten : ∀ (chunk : ℕ) (rows : List NobleFoundation.Row) (remaining : ℕ) (acc : List NobleFoundation.Row), (NobleFoundation.chunksOfGo chunk rows remaining acc).flatten = acc.reverse ++ rows

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.chunking_does_not_change_the_value
theorems.claim: the chunked staging evaluates exactly the ordered map of independent row runs
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.chunking_does_not_change_the_value : ∀ (chunk : ℕ) (rows : List NobleFoundation.Row), List.map NobleFoundation.rowRun (NobleFoundation.chunksOf chunk rows).flatten = NobleFoundation.evalBatch rows

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.node_work_is_staging_independent
theorems.claim: both declared stagings evaluate one operation per row, so staging cannot be mistaken for node work
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.node_work_is_staging_independent : ∀ (rows : List NobleFoundation.Row) (chunk : ℕ), (NobleFoundation.rowMajorCost rows.length).nodeWork = (NobleFoundation.chunkedCost chunk rows).nodeWork

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.chunked_writes_are_one_per_chunk
theorems.claim: the chunked staging's output writes are exactly its chunk count
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.chunked_writes_are_one_per_chunk : ∀ (chunk : ℕ) (rows : List NobleFoundation.Row), (NobleFoundation.chunkedCost chunk rows).stagingWrites = (NobleFoundation.chunksOf chunk rows).length

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.every_chunk_is_bounded_by_the_chunk_size
theorems.claim: each committed chunk holds at most one chunk of rows at a positive chunk size
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.every_chunk_is_bounded_by_the_chunk_size : ∀ (chunk : ℕ), 1 ≤ chunk → ∀ (rows : List NobleFoundation.Row) (remaining : ℕ) (acc : List NobleFoundation.Row), acc.length + remaining = chunk → ∀ staged ∈ NobleFoundation.chunksOfGo chunk rows remaining acc, staged.length ≤ chunk

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.live_row_slots_are_bounded_by_the_chunk
theorems.claim: a staging pass holds at most one chunk of live row slots
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.live_row_slots_are_bounded_by_the_chunk : ∀ (rows : List NobleFoundation.Row) (chunk : ℕ), (List.take chunk rows).length ≤ chunk

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.a_zero_chunk_drops_no_row
theorems.claim: a zero chunk size degenerates to one row per chunk and still covers every row
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.a_zero_chunk_drops_no_row : ∀ (rows : List NobleFoundation.Row), (NobleFoundation.chunksOf 0 rows).flatten = rows ∧ List.map NobleFoundation.rowRun (NobleFoundation.chunksOf 0 rows).flatten = NobleFoundation.evalBatch rows

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.pow2Int_rat
theorems.claim: a nonnegative model power equals the corresponding exact rational power
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.pow2Int_rat : ∀ (k : ℤ), 0 ≤ k → ↑(NobleFoundation.Binary32.pow2Int k) = 2 ^ k

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.quotient_round_error
theorems.claim: nearest ties-to-even quotient rounding is within one half denominator
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.quotient_round_error : ∀ (q r d n : ℕ), r < d → q * d + r = n → have rounded := if 2 * r > d then q + 1 else if 2 * r = d then q + q % 2 else q; 2 * NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.natAbsDiff (rounded * d) n ≤ d

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.nat_error_to_rat
theorems.claim: the integer quotient error rule converts to an exact rational half-denominator bound
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.nat_error_to_rat : ∀ (u d n : ℕ), 0 < d → 2 * NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.natAbsDiff (u * d) n ≤ d → |↑u - ↑n / ↑d| ≤ 1 / 2

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.roundNearest_error
theorems.claim: roundNearest has an exact rational half-denominator error bound
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.roundNearest_error : ∀ (n d : ℕ), 0 < d → |↑(NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.roundNearest n d) - ↑n / ↑d| ≤ 1 / 2

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.scalePair_den_pos
theorems.claim: positive input denominators remain positive after binary scaling
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.scalePair_den_pos : ∀ (a b : ℕ), 0 < b → 0 < (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.scalePair a b).2

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.scaled_exact_ratio
theorems.claim: undoing the scale factor recovers the original exact positive rational
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.scaled_exact_ratio : ∀ (a b : ℕ), 0 < b → have e := NobleFoundation.Binary32.floorLog2Ratio a b; have scaled := NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.scalePair a b; ↑scaled.1 / ↑scaled.2 * 2 ^ (e - 23) = ↑a / ↑b

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.roundNearest_bounds
theorems.claim: a scaled quotient in one normal significand bin rounds within that bin
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.roundNearest_bounds : ∀ (n d : ℕ), 0 < d → 2 ^ 23 * d ≤ n → n < 2 ^ 24 * d → 2 ^ 23 ≤ NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.roundNearest n d ∧ NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.roundNearest n d ≤ 2 ^ 24

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.roundedQuotient_bounds
theorems.claim: the model scaled quotient inherits the normal significand bounds
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.roundedQuotient_bounds : ∀ (a b : ℕ), 0 < b → 2 ^ 23 * (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.scalePair a b).2 ≤ (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.scalePair a b).1 → (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.scalePair a b).1 < 2 ^ 24 * (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.scalePair a b).2 → 2 ^ 23 ≤ NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.roundedQuotient a b ∧ NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.roundedQuotient a b ≤ 2 ^ 24

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.carry_value
theorems.claim: the significand carry preserves the represented exact dyadic value
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.carry_value : ∀ (e : ℤ) (rounded : ℕ), (if rounded = NobleFoundation.Binary32.pow2 24 then ↑(NobleFoundation.Binary32.pow2 23) * 2 ^ (e + 1 - 23) else ↑rounded * 2 ^ (e - 23)) = ↑rounded * 2 ^ (e - 23)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.carriedPair_m_bounds
theorems.claim: the carried significand remains in the normal encoding range
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.carriedPair_m_bounds : ∀ (a b : ℕ), 0 < b → 2 ^ 23 * (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.scalePair a b).2 ≤ (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.scalePair a b).1 → (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.scalePair a b).1 < 2 ^ 24 * (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.scalePair a b).2 → 2 ^ 23 ≤ (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.carriedPair a b).1 ∧ (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.carriedPair a b).1 < 2 ^ 24

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.roundPositive_eq_roundedNormalBits
theorems.claim: normal finite roundPositive output agrees with its encoded carried pair
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.roundPositive_eq_roundedNormalBits : ∀ (a b : ℕ), -126 ≤ (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.carriedPair a b).2 → (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.carriedPair a b).2 ≤ 127 → BitVec.ofNat 32 (NobleFoundation.Binary32.roundPositive a b) = NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.roundedNormalBits a b

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.normalEncoding_scaledMagnitude
theorems.claim: a bounded normal encoding decodes to its exact significand and exponent
theorems.statement: @NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.normalEncoding_scaledMagnitude : ∀ {e : ℤ} {m : ℕ}, -126 ≤ e → e ≤ 127 → 2 ^ 23 ≤ m → m < 2 ^ 24 → NobleFoundation.Binary32.scaledMagnitude (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.normalEncoding e m) = (m, e - 23)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.normalEncoding_not_negative
theorems.claim: a bounded normal encoding has a positive sign bit
theorems.statement: @NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.normalEncoding_not_negative : ∀ {e : ℤ} {m : ℕ}, -126 ≤ e → e ≤ 127 → 2 ^ 23 ≤ m → m < 2 ^ 24 → NobleFoundation.Binary32.isNegative (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.normalEncoding e m) = false

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.roundPositive_normal_absolute_error
theorems.claim: positive normal-range roundPositive has a universal half-ulp absolute bound under explicit scale premises
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.roundPositive_normal_absolute_error : ∀ (a b : ℕ), 0 < a → 0 < b → 2 ^ 23 * (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.scalePair a b).2 ≤ (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.scalePair a b).1 → (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.scalePair a b).1 < 2 ^ 24 * (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.scalePair a b).2 → -126 ≤ (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.carriedPair a b).2 → (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.carriedPair a b).2 ≤ 127 → |NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue (BitVec.ofNat 32 (NobleFoundation.Binary32.roundPositive a b)) - ↑a / ↑b| ≤ 1 / 2 * 2 ^ (NobleFoundation.Binary32.floorLog2Ratio a b - 23)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.roundPositive_normal_relative_error
theorems.claim: the normal half-ulp bound becomes relative under the bin lower endpoint premise
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.roundPositive_normal_relative_error : ∀ (a b : ℕ), 0 < a → 0 < b → 2 ^ 23 * (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.scalePair a b).2 ≤ (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.scalePair a b).1 → (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.scalePair a b).1 < 2 ^ 24 * (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.scalePair a b).2 → -126 ≤ (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.carriedPair a b).2 → (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.carriedPair a b).2 ≤ 127 → 2 ^ NobleFoundation.Binary32.floorLog2Ratio a b ≤ ↑a / ↑b → |NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue (BitVec.ofNat 32 (NobleFoundation.Binary32.roundPositive a b)) - ↑a / ↑b| ≤ 1 / 2 ^ 24 * (↑a / ↑b)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue_normalEncoding
theorems.claim: every bounded normal encoding has its exact rational dyadic value
theorems.statement: @NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue_normalEncoding : ∀ {e : ℤ} {m : ℕ}, -126 ≤ e → e ≤ 127 → 2 ^ 23 ≤ m → m < 2 ^ 24 → NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.normalEncoding e m) = ↑m * 2 ^ (e - 23)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.normal_error_applies_to_one_third

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.log2_eq
theorems.claim: the model log2 is the core floor logarithm
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.log2_eq : ∀ (n : ℕ), NobleFoundation.Binary32.log2 n = n.log2

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.log2_bracket
theorems.claim: the model log2 of a positive input brackets it between consecutive powers of two
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.log2_bracket : ∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < n → 2 ^ NobleFoundation.Binary32.log2 n ≤ n ∧ n < 2 ^ (NobleFoundation.Binary32.log2 n + 1)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.floorLog2Ratio_lower
theorems.claim: for every positive input 2^floorLog2Ratio times the denominator is at most the numerator
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.floorLog2Ratio_lower : ∀ (a b : ℕ), 0 < a → 0 < b → 2 ^ NobleFoundation.Binary32.floorLog2Ratio a b * ↑b ≤ ↑a

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.floorLog2Ratio_upper
theorems.claim: off the power boundary the numerator is strictly below 2^(floorLog2Ratio+1) times the denominator
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.floorLog2Ratio_upper : ∀ (a b : ℕ), 0 < a → 0 < b → ¬NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.powerBoundary a b → ↑a < 2 ^ (NobleFoundation.Binary32.floorLog2Ratio a b + 1) * ↑b

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.floorLog2Ratio_boundary
theorems.claim: on the power boundary the ratio is exactly 2^(floorLog2Ratio+1)
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.floorLog2Ratio_boundary : ∀ (a b : ℕ), NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.powerBoundary a b → ↑a = 2 ^ (NobleFoundation.Binary32.floorLog2Ratio a b + 1) * ↑b

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.scaled_ratio
theorems.claim: the scaled quotient is the exact ratio times 2^(23 - floorLog2Ratio)
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.scaled_ratio : ∀ (a b : ℕ), 0 < b → ↑(NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.scalePair a b).1 / ↑(NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.scalePair a b).2 = ↑a / ↑b * 2 ^ (23 - NobleFoundation.Binary32.floorLog2Ratio a b)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.scale_powers
theorems.claim: the scale exponents combine to 2^23 at the lower and 2^24 at the upper bin edge
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.scale_powers : ∀ (e : ℤ), 2 ^ e * 2 ^ (23 - e) = 2 ^ 23 ∧ 2 ^ (e + 1) * 2 ^ (23 - e) = 2 ^ 24

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.scale_lower
theorems.claim: the lower normal-bin scale premise holds for every positive input
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.scale_lower : ∀ (a b : ℕ), 0 < a → 0 < b → 2 ^ 23 * (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.scalePair a b).2 ≤ (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.scalePair a b).1

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.scale_upper
theorems.claim: the upper normal-bin scale premise holds for every positive input off the power boundary
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.scale_upper : ∀ (a b : ℕ), 0 < a → 0 < b → ¬NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.powerBoundary a b → (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.scalePair a b).1 < 2 ^ 24 * (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.scalePair a b).2

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.scale_at_boundary
theorems.claim: on the power boundary the scaled quotient is exactly 2^24 times its denominator
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.scale_at_boundary : ∀ (a b : ℕ), 0 < b → NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.powerBoundary a b → (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.scalePair a b).1 = 2 ^ 24 * (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.scalePair a b).2

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.upper_premise_fails_for_one_half
theorems.claim: the upper scale premise is not universal: 1/2 is on the power boundary and fails it
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.upper_premise_fails_for_one_half : NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.powerBoundary 1 2 ∧ ¬(NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.scalePair 1 2).1 < 2 ^ 24 * (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.scalePair 1 2).2

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.boundary_rounded
theorems.claim: on the power boundary the rounded significand is exactly 2^24
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.boundary_rounded : ∀ (a b : ℕ), 0 < b → NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.powerBoundary a b → NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.roundedQuotient a b = NobleFoundation.Binary32.pow2 24

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.boundary_rounds_exactly
theorems.claim: on the power boundary the carried normal result is the exact ratio
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.boundary_rounds_exactly : ∀ (a b : ℕ), 0 < b → NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.powerBoundary a b → -126 ≤ (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.carriedPair a b).2 → (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.carriedPair a b).2 ≤ 127 → NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue (BitVec.ofNat 32 (NobleFoundation.Binary32.roundPositive a b)) = ↑a / ↑b

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.roundPositive_absolute_error
theorems.claim: every positive input with a normal-range carried exponent has the half-ulp absolute bound, with no scale premise
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.roundPositive_absolute_error : ∀ (a b : ℕ), 0 < a → 0 < b → -126 ≤ (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.carriedPair a b).2 → (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.carriedPair a b).2 ≤ 127 → |NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue (BitVec.ofNat 32 (NobleFoundation.Binary32.roundPositive a b)) - ↑a / ↑b| ≤ 1 / 2 * 2 ^ (NobleFoundation.Binary32.floorLog2Ratio a b - 23)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.roundPositive_relative_error
theorems.claim: every positive input with a normal-range carried exponent has the 2^-24 relative bound, with no scale or bin premise
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.roundPositive_relative_error : ∀ (a b : ℕ), 0 < a → 0 < b → -126 ≤ (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.carriedPair a b).2 → (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.carriedPair a b).2 ≤ 127 → |NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue (BitVec.ofNat 32 (NobleFoundation.Binary32.roundPositive a b)) - ↑a / ↑b| ≤ 1 / 2 ^ 24 * (↑a / ↑b)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.absolute_error_covers_one_half
theorems.claim: at 1/2, where the upper premise fails, the result is exact and the absolute bound holds
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Scale.absolute_error_covers_one_half : NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue (BitVec.ofNat 32 (NobleFoundation.Binary32.roundPositive 1 2)) = 1 / 2 ∧ |NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue (BitVec.ofNat 32 (NobleFoundation.Binary32.roundPositive 1 2)) - 1 / 2| ≤ 1 / 2 * 2 ^ (NobleFoundation.Binary32.floorLog2Ratio 1 2 - 23)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Mutations.adjointAfterWith_stepCoefficient
theorems.claim: the reverse sweep parameterised by its update rule is exactly adjointAfter under the model rule
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Mutations.adjointAfterWith_stepCoefficient : ∀ (graph : NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Graph) (values seed : ℕ → ℝ) (fuel : ℕ), NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Mutations.adjointAfterWith NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.stepCoefficient graph values seed fuel = NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.adjointAfter graph values seed fuel

theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Mutations.slotGraph_addDropsSecond_caught : NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Mutations.slotGradientWith NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Mutations.addDropsSecond NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.slotGraph NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.slotGraphValues (NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.slotGraphSeed 1) 0 = 0 ∧ NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Mutations.slotGradientWith NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Mutations.addDropsSecond NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.slotGraph NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.slotGraphValues (NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.slotGraphSeed 1) 1 = 1 ∧ NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.tangent NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.slotGraph NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.slotGraphInputs (fun x => 0) (NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.slotGraphDirection 0) (fun x => 0) 7 ≠ 0 ∧ NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.tangent NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.slotGraph NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.slotGraphInputs (fun x => 0) (NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.slotGraphDirection 1) (fun x => 0) 7 ≠ 1

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Mutations.slotGraph_repeatedCountedOnce_caught

theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Mutations.slotGraph_repeatedCountedOnce_caught : NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Mutations.slotGradientWith NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Mutations.repeatedCountedOnce NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.slotGraph NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.slotGraphValues (NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.slotGraphSeed 1) 0 = 17 ∧ NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Mutations.slotGradientWith NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Mutations.repeatedCountedOnce NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.slotGraph NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.slotGraphValues (NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.slotGraphSeed 1) 1 = 24 ∧ NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.tangent NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.slotGraph NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.slotGraphInputs (fun x => 0) (NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.slotGraphDirection 1) (fun x => 0) 7 ≠ 24
