theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Ownership.step_iff_wordRule
theorems.claim: the executable step agrees exactly with one independent rule per word stated from the fragment prose
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Ownership.step_iff_wordRule : ∀ (word : NobleFoundation.Ownership.Word) (operands out : List NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload), NobleFoundation.Ownership.step word operands = some out ↔ NobleFoundation.Ownership.WordRule word operands out

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Ownership.judged_iff_accounts
theorems.claim: the judgment built on the independent per-word rules coincides with Accounts
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Ownership.judged_iff_accounts : ∀ (program : NobleFoundation.Ownership.Program) (start out : List NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload), NobleFoundation.Ownership.Judged program start out ↔ NobleFoundation.Ownership.Accounts program start out

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Ownership.run_complete
theorems.claim: every Accounts derivation is a checker acceptance
theorems.statement: @NobleFoundation.Ownership.run_complete : ∀ {program : NobleFoundation.Ownership.Program} {start out : List NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload}, NobleFoundation.Ownership.Accounts program start out → NobleFoundation.Ownership.run program start = some out

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Ownership.run_iff_judged
theorems.claim: the checker decides the independent judgment exactly
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Ownership.run_iff_judged : ∀ (program : NobleFoundation.Ownership.Program) (start out : List NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload), NobleFoundation.Ownership.run program start = some out ↔ NobleFoundation.Ownership.Judged program start out

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Ownership.step_preserves_agreement
theorems.claim: one step preserves eligibility agreement on the stacks it admits in both arms
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Ownership.step_preserves_agreement : ∀ (word : NobleFoundation.Ownership.Word) {left right left' right' : List NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload}, NobleFoundation.Ownership.EligibilityAgrees left right → NobleFoundation.Ownership.step word left = some left' → NobleFoundation.Ownership.step word right = some right' → NobleFoundation.Ownership.EligibilityAgrees left' right'

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Ownership.joined_sequence_admission_agrees
theorems.claim: on a straight-line program two eligibility-agreeing stacks are admitted in both arms or neither and leave agreeing stacks
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Ownership.joined_sequence_admission_agrees : ∀ (program : NobleFoundation.Ownership.Program), NobleFoundation.Ownership.StraightLine program → ∀ (left right : List NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload), NobleFoundation.Ownership.EligibilityAgrees left right → (NobleFoundation.Ownership.run program left).isSome = (NobleFoundation.Ownership.run program right).isSome ∧ ∀ (left' right' : List NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload), NobleFoundation.Ownership.run program left = some left' → NobleFoundation.Ownership.run program right = some right' → NobleFoundation.Ownership.EligibilityAgrees left' right'

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Ownership.joined_judgment_transfers
theorems.claim: a straight-line judgment carries over to any eligibility-agreeing start with agreeing results
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Ownership.joined_judgment_transfers : ∀ (program : NobleFoundation.Ownership.Program), NobleFoundation.Ownership.StraightLine program → ∀ {left right left' : List NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload}, NobleFoundation.Ownership.EligibilityAgrees left right → NobleFoundation.Ownership.Judged program left left' → ∃ right', NobleFoundation.Ownership.Judged program right right' ∧ NobleFoundation.Ownership.EligibilityAgrees left' right'

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Ownership.equal_length_does_not_lift
theorems.claim: equal-length stacks that disagree on eligibility separate a straight-line dup
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Ownership.equal_length_does_not_lift : [NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload.data 1].length = [NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload.resource 1].length ∧ (NobleFoundation.Ownership.run (NobleFoundation.Ownership.Program.word NobleFoundation.Ownership.Word.dup) [NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload.data 1]).isSome = true ∧ (NobleFoundation.Ownership.run (NobleFoundation.Ownership.Program.word NobleFoundation.Ownership.Word.dup) [NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload.resource 1]).isSome = false

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Ownership.lift_fixture
theorems.claim: stacks with different owners but agreeing eligibility run a three-word sequence alike and agree again
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Ownership.lift_fixture : NobleFoundation.Ownership.run ((NobleFoundation.Ownership.Program.word NobleFoundation.Ownership.Word.swap).compose ((NobleFoundation.Ownership.Program.word NobleFoundation.Ownership.Word.dup).compose (NobleFoundation.Ownership.Program.word NobleFoundation.Ownership.Word.drop))) [NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload.resource 1, NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload.data 2] = some [NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload.data 2, NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload.resource 1] ∧ NobleFoundation.Ownership.run ((NobleFoundation.Ownership.Program.word NobleFoundation.Ownership.Word.swap).compose ((NobleFoundation.Ownership.Program.word NobleFoundation.Ownership.Word.dup).compose (NobleFoundation.Ownership.Program.word NobleFoundation.Ownership.Word.drop))) [NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload.resource 9, (NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload.data 3).wrapped] = some [(NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload.data 3).wrapped, NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload.resource 9] ∧ NobleFoundation.Ownership.EligibilityAgrees [NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload.data 2, NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload.resource 1] [(NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload.data 3).wrapped, NobleFoundation.Ownership.Payload.resource 9]

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.floorLog2Ratio_le_carried
theorems.claim: the carried exponent is at least the scale exponent
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.floorLog2Ratio_le_carried : ∀ (a b : ℕ), NobleFoundation.Binary32.floorLog2Ratio a b ≤ (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.carriedPair a b).2

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.floorLog2Ratio_upper_le
theorems.claim: for every positive input the numerator is at most 2^(floorLog2Ratio+1) times the denominator
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.floorLog2Ratio_upper_le : ∀ (a b : ℕ), 0 < a → 0 < b → ↑a ≤ 2 ^ (NobleFoundation.Binary32.floorLog2Ratio a b + 1) * ↑b

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.subnormal_numerator_bound
theorems.claim: below the normal range the subnormal numerator a * 2^149 is at most 2^23 denominators
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.subnormal_numerator_bound : ∀ (a b : ℕ), 0 < a → 0 < b → (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.carriedPair a b).2 < -126 → a * NobleFoundation.Binary32.pow2 149 ≤ 2 ^ 23 * b

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.subnormal_significand_bound
theorems.claim: below the normal range the rounded subnormal significand is at most 2^23
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.subnormal_significand_bound : ∀ (a b : ℕ), 0 < a → 0 < b → (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.carriedPair a b).2 < -126 → NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.roundNearest (a * NobleFoundation.Binary32.pow2 149) b ≤ 2 ^ 23

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.roundPositive_subnormal
theorems.claim: below the normal range roundPositive is the rounded significand capped at the smallest normal
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.roundPositive_subnormal : ∀ (a b : ℕ), (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.carriedPair a b).2 < -126 → NobleFoundation.Binary32.roundPositive a b = if NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.roundNearest (a * NobleFoundation.Binary32.pow2 149) b ≥ NobleFoundation.Binary32.pow2 23 then NobleFoundation.Binary32.pow2 23 else NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.roundNearest (a * NobleFoundation.Binary32.pow2 149) b

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.roundPositive_eq_significand
theorems.claim: below the normal range the cap never changes the rounded significand
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.roundPositive_eq_significand : ∀ (a b : ℕ), 0 < a → 0 < b → (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.carriedPair a b).2 < -126 → NobleFoundation.Binary32.roundPositive a b = NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.roundNearest (a * NobleFoundation.Binary32.pow2 149) b

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.subnormal_scaledMagnitude
theorems.claim: a significand below 2^23 encodes the subnormal n * 2^-149
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.subnormal_scaledMagnitude : ∀ n < 2 ^ 23, NobleFoundation.Binary32.scaledMagnitude (BitVec.ofNat 32 n) = (n, -149)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.smallest_normal_scaledMagnitude
theorems.claim: the significand 2^23 encodes the smallest normal with value 2^23 * 2^-149
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.smallest_normal_scaledMagnitude : NobleFoundation.Binary32.scaledMagnitude (BitVec.ofNat 32 (2 ^ 23)) = (2 ^ 23, -149)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.small_encoding_not_negative
theorems.claim: a significand of at most 2^23 encodes a positive sign
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.small_encoding_not_negative : ∀ n ≤ 2 ^ 23, NobleFoundation.Binary32.isNegative (BitVec.ofNat 32 n) = false

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.exactValue_small
theorems.claim: every significand of at most 2^23 encodes exactly n * 2^-149
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.exactValue_small : ∀ n ≤ 2 ^ 23, NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue (BitVec.ofNat 32 n) = ↑n * 2 ^ (-149)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.roundPositive_subnormal_absolute_error
theorems.claim: below the normal range the encoded result is within 2^-150 of the exact quotient
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.roundPositive_subnormal_absolute_error : ∀ (a b : ℕ), 0 < a → 0 < b → (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.carriedPair a b).2 < -126 → |NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue (BitVec.ofNat 32 (NobleFoundation.Binary32.roundPositive a b)) - ↑a / ↑b| ≤ 1 / 2 * 2 ^ (-149)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.roundPositive_finite_absolute_error
theorems.claim: every positive input with a finite result is within half the spacing of its binade, 2^(max e -126 - 23)
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.roundPositive_finite_absolute_error : ∀ (a b : ℕ), 0 < a → 0 < b → (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.carriedPair a b).2 ≤ 127 → |NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue (BitVec.ofNat 32 (NobleFoundation.Binary32.roundPositive a b)) - ↑a / ↑b| ≤ 1 / 2 * 2 ^ (max (NobleFoundation.Binary32.floorLog2Ratio a b) (-126) - 23)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.subnormal_rule_applies_below_the_normal_range
theorems.claim: non-vacuity: 1/(3*2^130) rounds to the subnormal significand 174763 within the subnormal bound
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.subnormal_rule_applies_below_the_normal_range : (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.carriedPair 1 (3 * 2 ^ 130)).2 < -126 ∧ NobleFoundation.Binary32.roundPositive 1 (3 * 2 ^ 130) = 174763 ∧ |NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue (BitVec.ofNat 32 (NobleFoundation.Binary32.roundPositive 1 (3 * 2 ^ 130))) - 1 / ↑(3 * 2 ^ 130)| ≤ 1 / 2 * 2 ^ (-149)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.rounding_to_the_smallest_normal_attains_the_bound
theorems.claim: a tie halfway below 2^-126 rounds to the smallest normal with error exactly 2^-150
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.rounding_to_the_smallest_normal_attains_the_bound : (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.carriedPair (2 ^ 24 - 1) (2 ^ 150)).2 < -126 ∧ NobleFoundation.Binary32.roundPositive (2 ^ 24 - 1) (2 ^ 150) = 2 ^ 23 ∧ |NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue (BitVec.ofNat 32 (NobleFoundation.Binary32.roundPositive (2 ^ 24 - 1) (2 ^ 150))) - ↑(2 ^ 24 - 1) / ↑(2 ^ 150)| = 1 / 2 * 2 ^ (-149)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.subnormal_results_are_not_relatively_bounded
theorems.claim: a subnormal result with relative error one third shows the subnormal rule must be absolute
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.Binary32.Subnormal.subnormal_results_are_not_relatively_bounded : (NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.carriedPair 3 (2 ^ 151)).2 < -126 ∧ 1 / 2 ^ 24 * (3 / ↑(2 ^ 151)) < |NobleFoundation.Binary32.Error.exactValue (BitVec.ofNat 32 (NobleFoundation.Binary32.roundPositive 3 (2 ^ 151))) - 3 / ↑(2 ^ 151)|

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Transpose.valuesUpTo_stable
theorems.claim: a prefix value is final once computed: every later prefix gives the node value
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Transpose.valuesUpTo_stable : ∀ (graph : NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Graph) (is ip : ℕ → ℝ) (count index : ℕ), index < count → NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.valuesUpTo graph is ip count index = NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.value graph is ip index

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Transpose.tangentUpTo_stable
theorems.claim: a prefix tangent is final once computed: every later prefix gives the node tangent
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Transpose.tangentUpTo_stable : ∀ (graph : NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Graph) (is ip ds dp : ℕ → ℝ) (count index : ℕ), index < count → NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.tangentUpTo graph is ip ds dp count index = NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.tangent graph is ip ds dp index

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Transpose.stepCoefficient_of_not_operand
theorems.claim: a node assigns no partial-derivative coefficient to an index that is not one of its operands
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Transpose.stepCoefficient_of_not_operand : ∀ (values : ℕ → ℝ) (node : NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Node), ∀ index ∉ node.operands, NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.stepCoefficient values node index = 0

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Transpose.coefficients_pair_to_the_tangent
theorems.claim: for a node with operands, its coefficients paired with the operand tangents give its own tangent
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Transpose.coefficients_pair_to_the_tangent : ∀ (graph : NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Graph), NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.WellFormed graph → ∀ (is ip ds dp : ℕ → ℝ) (bound consumer : ℕ), consumer < bound → (graph.node consumer).operands ≠ [] → ∑ index ∈ Finset.range bound, NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.stepCoefficient (NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.value graph is ip) (graph.node consumer) index * NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.tangent graph is ip ds dp index = NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.tangent graph is ip ds dp consumer

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Transpose.leaf_coefficients_vanish
theorems.claim: a node without operands assigns every index the coefficient zero
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Transpose.leaf_coefficients_vanish : ∀ (values : ℕ → ℝ) (node : NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Node), node.operands = [] → ∀ (index : ℕ), NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.stepCoefficient values node index = 0

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Transpose.frontier_succ
theorems.claim: one reverse step moves only the processed consumer with operands out of the frontier
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Transpose.frontier_succ : ∀ (graph : NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Graph) (tangents : ℕ → ℝ) (fuel index : ℕ), fuel + 1 ≤ graph.arity → NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Transpose.frontier graph tangents fuel index = if graph.arity - 1 - fuel = index ∧ (graph.node index).operands ≠ [] then tangents index else NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Transpose.frontier graph tangents (fuel + 1) index

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Transpose.frontier_invariant
theorems.claim: after any number of reverse steps the adjoints paired with the frontier weights equal the seed paired with every tangent
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Transpose.frontier_invariant : ∀ (graph : NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Graph), NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.WellFormed graph → ∀ (is ip ds dp seed : ℕ → ℝ), ∀ fuel ≤ graph.arity, NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.adjointDot graph (NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.adjointAfter graph (NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.value graph is ip) seed fuel) (NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Transpose.frontier graph (NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.tangent graph is ip ds dp) fuel) = NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.adjointDot graph seed (NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.tangent graph is ip ds dp)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Transpose.transpose_identity
theorems.claim: for every well-formed graph the full sweep leaf adjoints paired with their tangents equal the seed paired with every tangent
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Transpose.transpose_identity : ∀ (graph : NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Graph), NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.WellFormed graph → ∀ (is ip ds dp seed : ℕ → ℝ), (∑ index ∈ Finset.range graph.arity, if (graph.node index).operands = [] then NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.adjointAfter graph (NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.value graph is ip) seed graph.arity index * NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.tangent graph is ip ds dp index else 0) = ∑ index ∈ Finset.range graph.arity, seed index * NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.tangent graph is ip ds dp index

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Transpose.reverse_sweep_is_the_derivative
theorems.claim: with a unit seed on any output of a well-formed graph the leaf adjoint pairing is the Mathlib derivative of that output
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Transpose.reverse_sweep_is_the_derivative : ∀ (graph : NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Graph), NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.WellFormed graph → ∀ (is ip ds dp : ℕ → ℝ), ∀ output < graph.arity, HasDerivAt (fun t => NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.value graph (NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.line is ds t) (NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.line ip dp t) output) (∑ index ∈ Finset.range graph.arity, if (graph.node index).operands = [] then NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.adjointAfter graph (NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.value graph is ip) (NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Transpose.unitSeed output) graph.arity index * NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.tangent graph is ip ds dp index else 0) 0

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Transpose.slotGraph_transpose
theorems.claim: non-vacuity: on slotGraph the full sweep with seed one pairs the leaves to the slot-zero tangent 17
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Transpose.slotGraph_transpose : (∑ index ∈ Finset.range NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.slotGraph.arity, if (NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.slotGraph.node index).operands = [] then NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.adjointAfter NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.slotGraph (NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.value NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.slotGraph NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.slotGraphInputs fun x => 0) (NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.slotGraphSeed 1) NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.slotGraph.arity index * NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.tangent NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.slotGraph NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.slotGraphInputs (fun x => 0) (NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.slotGraphDirection 0) (fun x => 0) index else 0) = 17

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Adjoint.adjointAfter_unrolled
theorems.claim: the reverse sweep unrolls to the seed plus every processed step contribution, each made with the processed node adjoint at its own step
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Adjoint.adjointAfter_unrolled : ∀ (graph : NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Graph) (values seed : ℕ → ℝ) (fuel index : ℕ), NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.adjointAfter graph values seed fuel index = seed index + ∑ step ∈ Finset.range fuel, NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.contribution values (NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.adjointAfter graph values seed step (graph.arity - 1 - step)) (graph.node (graph.arity - 1 - step)) index

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Adjoint.adjoint_step_frame
theorems.claim: on a well-formed graph one reverse step leaves every adjoint at or above the processed node unchanged
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Adjoint.adjoint_step_frame : ∀ (graph : NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Graph), NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.WellFormed graph → ∀ (values seed : ℕ → ℝ) (fuel index : ℕ), graph.arity - 1 - fuel ≤ index → NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.adjointAfter graph values seed (fuel + 1) index = NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.adjointAfter graph values seed fuel index

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Adjoint.adjoint_final_once_processed
theorems.claim: on a well-formed graph a node adjoint is final once the sweep has processed it
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Adjoint.adjoint_final_once_processed : ∀ (graph : NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Graph), NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.WellFormed graph → ∀ (values seed : ℕ → ℝ) (fuel index : ℕ), graph.arity - 1 - fuel ≤ index → ∀ (extra : ℕ), NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.adjointAfter graph values seed (fuel + extra) index = NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.adjointAfter graph values seed fuel index

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Adjoint.processed_adjoint_is_final
theorems.claim: on a well-formed graph the adjoint a node contributes with is its final adjoint
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Adjoint.processed_adjoint_is_final : ∀ (graph : NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Graph), NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.WellFormed graph → ∀ (values seed : ℕ → ℝ), ∀ step < graph.arity, NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.adjointAfter graph values seed step (graph.arity - 1 - step) = NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.adjointAfter graph values seed graph.arity (graph.arity - 1 - step)

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Adjoint.final_adjoint_eq
theorems.claim: on a well-formed graph every final adjoint is its seed plus, over every node, that node final adjoint times its coefficient for this node
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Adjoint.final_adjoint_eq : ∀ (graph : NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Graph), NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.WellFormed graph → ∀ (values seed : ℕ → ℝ) (index : ℕ), NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.adjointAfter graph values seed graph.arity index = seed index + ∑ consumer ∈ Finset.range graph.arity, NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.contribution values (NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.adjointAfter graph values seed graph.arity consumer) (graph.node consumer) index

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Adjoint.final_adjoint_eq_seed_plus_consumers
theorems.claim: on a well-formed graph every final adjoint is its seed plus its consumers contributions, each with the consumer final adjoint
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Adjoint.final_adjoint_eq_seed_plus_consumers : ∀ (graph : NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Graph), NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.WellFormed graph → ∀ (values seed : ℕ → ℝ) (index : ℕ), NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.adjointAfter graph values seed graph.arity index = seed index + ∑ consumer ∈ Finset.range graph.arity with index ∈ (graph.node consumer).operands, NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.contribution values (NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.adjointAfter graph values seed graph.arity consumer) (graph.node consumer) index

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Adjoint.unconsumed_final_adjoint_is_seed
theorems.claim: on a well-formed graph a node no node consumes keeps its seed as its final adjoint
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Adjoint.unconsumed_final_adjoint_is_seed : ∀ (graph : NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Graph), NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.WellFormed graph → ∀ (values seed : ℕ → ℝ) (index : ℕ), (∀ consumer < graph.arity, index ∉ (graph.node consumer).operands) → NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.adjointAfter graph values seed graph.arity index = seed index

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Adjoint.exampleGraph_final_adjoints
theorems.claim: with seed 1 on the output and 5 on the interior constant node the example graph final adjoints are 1, 8, 13 and 8
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Adjoint.exampleGraph_final_adjoints : NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.adjointAfter NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.exampleGraph NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.exampleGraphValues NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Adjoint.interiorSeed NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.exampleGraph.arity 3 = 1 ∧ NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.adjointAfter NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.exampleGraph NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.exampleGraphValues NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Adjoint.interiorSeed NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.exampleGraph.arity 2 = 8 ∧ NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.adjointAfter NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.exampleGraph NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.exampleGraphValues NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Adjoint.interiorSeed NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.exampleGraph.arity 1 = 13 ∧ NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.adjointAfter NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.exampleGraph NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.exampleGraphValues NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Adjoint.interiorSeed NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.exampleGraph.arity 0 = 8

theorems.name: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Adjoint.exampleGraph_node_one_is_seed_plus_consumer
theorems.claim: the example graph interior node adjoint is its seed 5 plus the addition contribution 8
theorems.statement: NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Adjoint.exampleGraph_node_one_is_seed_plus_consumer : NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.adjointAfter NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.exampleGraph NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.exampleGraphValues NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Adjoint.interiorSeed NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.exampleGraph.arity 1 = NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Adjoint.interiorSeed 1 + NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.contribution NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.exampleGraphValues (NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.adjointAfter NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.exampleGraph NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.exampleGraphValues NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.Adjoint.interiorSeed NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.exampleGraph.arity 2) (NobleFoundation.ReverseAD.exampleGraph.node 2) 1
